pyth-principles-001-answer.title: The right angle tells you where c goes
pyth-principles-001-answer.alt: State Pythagoras’ theorem for a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c. a² + b² = c². The hypotenuse c is opposite the right angle. Square both legs, then add. a² + b² = c²

pyth-principles-002-answer.title: Find 90°, then look across
steps: The opposite side is the hypotenuse.
Its position on the page does not matter.
pyth-principles-002-answer.alt: How do you identify the hypotenuse, even when a right triangle is drawn upside down? Find the right angle; the side opposite it is the hypotenuse and the longest side. The opposite side is the hypotenuse. Its position on the page does not matter.

pyth-principles-003-answer.title: The two legs can swap labels
pyth-principles-003-answer.alt: In a² + b² = c², why can a and b swap names but c cannot swap with a leg? Addition lets the legs swap; c must remain the hypotenuse opposite the right angle. a² + b² = b² + a² c always labels the hypotenuse.

pyth-principles-004-answer.title: A sketch is not evidence of 90°
steps: Look for a stated or established right angle.
Do not decide from appearance alone.
pyth-principles-004-answer.alt: A sketch looks right-angled but has no angle marking or measurements. Why is that insufficient for Pythagoras? A sketch is not proof. You need a stated, marked or established right angle. Look for a stated or established right angle. Do not decide from appearance alone.

pyth-principles-005-answer.title: The right-angle vertex is A
steps: The two sides touching A are the legs.
BC faces A, so BC is the hypotenuse.
pyth-principles-005-answer.alt: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A. Which side must be the hypotenuse? BC, because it is opposite the right angle at A. The two sides touching A are the legs. BC faces A, so BC is the hypotenuse.

pyth-principles-005-question.title: Sketch the problem
pyth-principles-005-question.alt: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A. Which side must be the hypotenuse?

pyth-principles-006-answer.title: Pythagoras compares square areas
steps: Area on leg a + area on leg b
equals the area on hypotenuse c.
pyth-principles-006-answer.alt: What does a² + b² = c² mean if you draw a square on each side of a right triangle? The areas of the two squares on the legs add to the area of the square on the hypotenuse. Area on leg a + area on leg b equals the area on hypotenuse c.

pyth-principles-007-answer.title: Missing hypotenuse: add the squares
pyth-principles-007-answer.alt: What formula finds a missing hypotenuse from known legs a and b? c = √(a² + b²): square, add, then take the square root. c² = a² + b² c = √(a² + b²)

pyth-principles-008-answer.title: Missing leg: subtract the squares
steps: a² + b² = c²  →  b² = c² − a²
pyth-principles-008-answer.alt: What formula finds missing leg b from hypotenuse c and other leg a? b = √(c² − a²): square, subtract, then take the square root. a² + b² = c²  →  b² = c² − a² b = √(c² − a²)

pyth-principles-009-answer.title: Remove the known leg’s square
pyth-principles-009-answer.alt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 17 cm and a leg 15 cm. Why subtract 15² from 17²? The hypotenuse square equals both leg squares combined; subtracting one leaves the other. b² = 17² − 15² = 289 − 225 = 64 b = √64 = 8 cm

pyth-principles-010-answer.title: A square is not yet a side length
steps: x = 9; a side length is positive.
pyth-principles-010-answer.alt: You find x² = 81 when calculating a triangle’s side. What is x? 9, because √81 = 9 and a side length is positive. x² = 81  →  x = √81 x = 9; a side length is positive.

pyth-principles-011-answer.title: Use one unit before squaring
pyth-principles-011-answer.alt: A right triangle’s legs are 300 cm and 4 m. Find its hypotenuse in metres. 5 m. First convert 300 cm to 3 m; then √(3² + 4²) = 5. 300 cm = 3 m c = √(3² + 4²) = 5 m

pyth-principles-012-answer.title: Square units become length units
pyth-principles-012-answer.alt: If c² = 25 cm², what is the hypotenuse length and its unit? c = 5 cm. Taking the square root converts squared centimetres back to centimetres. c² = 25 cm² c = √25 cm = 5 cm

pyth-principles-013-answer.title: Whole-number sides of a right triangle
pyth-principles-013-answer.alt: What is a Pythagorean triple? Three positive integers whose two smaller squares sum to the largest square. 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 25 = 5², so (3, 4, 5) is a triple.

pyth-principles-014-answer.title: Common triple: 3, 4, 5
pyth-principles-014-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse. 5: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5². 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 √25 = 5; the largest number goes opposite 90°.

pyth-principles-015-answer.title: Common triple: 5, 12, 13
pyth-principles-015-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse. 13: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13². 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 √169 = 13; the largest number goes opposite 90°.

pyth-principles-016-answer.title: Common triple: 8, 15, 17
pyth-principles-016-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 8 and 15. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse. 17: 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17². 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 √289 = 17; the largest number goes opposite 90°.

pyth-principles-017-answer.title: Common triple: 7, 24, 25
pyth-principles-017-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 7 and 24. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse. 25: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 √625 = 25; the largest number goes opposite 90°.

pyth-principles-018-answer.title: Common triple: 9, 40, 41
pyth-principles-018-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 9 and 40. Complete the common triple by giving its hypotenuse. 41: 9² + 40² = 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 41². 9² + 40² = 81 + 1600 = 1681 √1681 = 41; the largest number goes opposite 90°.

pyth-principles-019-answer.title: Scale the whole triple by 2
pyth-principles-019-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse. 10 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 2. (3, 4, 5) × 2 = (6, 8, 10) Check: 36 + 64 = 100.

pyth-principles-020-answer.title: Scale the whole triple by 3
pyth-principles-020-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse. 15 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 3. (3, 4, 5) × 3 = (9, 12, 15) Check: 81 + 144 = 225.

pyth-principles-021-answer.title: Scale the whole triple by 4
pyth-principles-021-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 12 cm and 16 cm. Use the 3–4–5 pattern to find its hypotenuse. 20 cm: multiply every side of 3–4–5 by 4. (3, 4, 5) × 4 = (12, 16, 20) Check: 144 + 256 = 400.

pyth-principles-022-answer.title: The pattern also works with decimals
pyth-principles-022-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 0.6 m and 0.8 m. Use a familiar side ratio to find its hypotenuse. 1 m: these are 3–4–5 lengths multiplied by 0.2. (3, 4, 5) × 0.2 = (0.6, 0.8, 1) 0.6² + 0.8² = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1

pyth-principles-023-answer.title: Scale every side by the same factor
pyth-principles-023-answer.alt: Why does multiplying every side of a Pythagorean triple by the same positive number preserve the right angle? Each square gains the same factor k², so a² + b² = c² remains true. (ka)² + (kb)² = k²(a² + b²) k²c² = (kc)²: the equation still holds.

pyth-principles-024-answer.title: Use the longest side as the test side
pyth-principles-024-answer.alt: How can side lengths 9, 12 and 15 establish that a triangle is right-angled? 9² + 12² = 15²; by the converse of Pythagoras, the angle opposite 15 is 90°. 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 15² = 225, so the opposite angle is 90°.

pyth-principles-025-answer.title: Similar-looking numbers may fail the test
pyth-principles-025-answer.alt: Why are 4, 5 and 6 not a Pythagorean triple? 4² + 5² = 41, but 6² = 36. The squares do not match. 4² + 5² = 16 + 25 = 41 6² = 36; 41 ≠ 36.

pyth-principles-026-answer.title: Some lengths stay as square roots
pyth-principles-026-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 5 cm and 5 cm. Give its hypotenuse exactly, without a decimal approximation. 5√2 cm: √(5² + 5²) = √50 = 5√2. c² = 25 + 25 = 50 c = √50 = 5√2 cm

pyth-principles-027-answer.title: The 45°–45°–90° side pattern
pyth-principles-027-answer.alt: A right isosceles triangle has equal legs x. What is its hypotenuse in terms of x? x√2, because c² = x² + x² = 2x². Equal legs: x and x Hypotenuse: √(2x²) = x√2

pyth-principles-028-answer.title: Round only the final length
pyth-principles-028-answer.alt: A right triangle has legs 8 cm and 11 cm. Find the hypotenuse to one decimal place. 13.6 cm: keep √185 unrounded until the final answer. c = √(8² + 11²) = √185 √185 ≈ 13.6015 → 13.6 cm

pyth-questions-001-answer.title: “Vertical wall” + “level ground” means 90°
steps: Wall and ground form the two legs.
pyth-questions-001-answer.alt: A ladder leans against a vertical wall on level ground. Which length represents the hypotenuse? The ladder’s length: the ladder is opposite the right angle between wall and ground. Wall and ground form the two legs. The ladder is the hypotenuse.

pyth-questions-002-answer.title: The ladder is given; find a leg
steps: h = 12 m; it must be less than 13 m.
pyth-questions-002-answer.alt: A 13 m ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is 5 m from the wall on level ground. How high does it reach? 12 m: h = √(13² − 5²) = √144. h² = 13² − 5² = 144 h = 12 m; it must be less than 13 m.

pyth-questions-002-question.title: Sketch the problem
pyth-questions-002-question.alt: A 13 m ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is 5 m from the wall on level ground. How high does it reach?

pyth-questions-003-answer.title: “Foot from the wall” is horizontal distance
pyth-questions-003-answer.alt: A 10 m ladder reaches 8 m up a vertical wall. How far is its foot from the wall on level ground? 6 m: d = √(10² − 8²) = √36. d² = 10² − 8² = 36 d = 6 m

pyth-questions-003-question.title: Sketch the problem
pyth-questions-003-question.alt: A 10 m ladder reaches 8 m up a vertical wall. How far is its foot from the wall on level ground?

pyth-questions-004-answer.title: A taut wire is a straight sloping side
pyth-questions-004-answer.alt: A taut wire joins the top of a 12 m vertical pole to an anchor 5 m from its base on level ground. Find the wire’s length. 13 m: the wire is the hypotenuse, so √(12² + 5²) = 13. wire² = 12² + 5² = 169 wire = 13 m

pyth-questions-005-answer.title: Known sloping length → subtract
pyth-questions-005-answer.alt: A taut 20 m wire runs from a 16 m vertical pole’s top to level ground. How far from the pole’s base is the anchor? 12 m: d = √(20² − 16²) = √144. d² = 20² − 16² = 144 d = 12 m

pyth-questions-006-answer.title: “Opposite corners” means a diagonal
steps: A rectangle’s corner supplies the right angle.
pyth-questions-006-answer.alt: A rectangular field is 8 m wide and 15 m long. Find the straight distance between opposite corners. 17 m: opposite corners are joined by the diagonal, √(8² + 15²). A rectangle’s corner supplies the right angle. d = √(8² + 15²) = 17 m

pyth-questions-007-answer.title: A square gives two equal legs
pyth-questions-007-answer.alt: A square courtyard has side 7 m. Find its diagonal to one decimal place. 9.9 m: d = √(7² + 7²) = 7√2 ≈ 9.8995. d² = 7² + 7² = 98 d = 7√2 ≈ 9.9 m

pyth-questions-008-answer.title: The diagonal is the hypotenuse
pyth-questions-008-answer.alt: A rectangular sign has diagonal 25 cm and height 7 cm. Find its width. 24 cm: w = √(25² − 7²) = √576. w² = 25² − 7² = 576 w = 24 cm

pyth-questions-008-question.title: Sketch the problem
pyth-questions-008-question.alt: A rectangular sign has diagonal 25 cm and height 7 cm. Find its width.

pyth-questions-009-answer.title: “Screen size” here means the diagonal
pyth-questions-009-answer.alt: A rectangular screen is 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. What is its corner-to-corner screen size? 50 cm: the diagonal follows the 3–4–5 pattern scaled by 10. (3, 4, 5) × 10 = (30, 40, 50) d = √(30² + 40²) = 50 cm

pyth-questions-010-answer.title: “Straight line” asks for displacement
steps: North and east form a right angle.
pyth-questions-010-answer.alt: You walk 6 km north, then 8 km east. How far are you from your starting point in a straight line? 10 km: north and east are perpendicular, so √(6² + 8²) = 10. North and east form a right angle. d = √(6² + 8²) = 10 km

pyth-questions-011-answer.title: “Distance walked” follows the route
steps: The straight shortcut is a different length.
pyth-questions-011-answer.alt: You walk 6 km north, then 8 km east. Why is the distance you actually walked 14 km, not 10 km? Travel distance adds the route’s two legs: 6 + 8 = 14 km. Ten kilometres is the direct shortcut. Add the journey: 6 + 8 = 14 km. The straight shortcut is a different length.

pyth-questions-012-answer.title: Changing compass direction does not change it
steps: West and north still meet at 90°.
pyth-questions-012-answer.alt: A boat travels 9 km west, then 12 km north. Find its straight-line distance from the start. 15 km: west and north are perpendicular, and 9–12–15 is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. West and north still meet at 90°. d = √(9² + 12²) = 15 km

pyth-questions-013-answer.title: Coordinate differences become the legs
pyth-questions-013-answer.alt: On a square coordinate grid, A is (1, 2) and B is (7, 10). Find the straight-line distance AB. 10 units: horizontal change 6, vertical change 8; √(6² + 8²) = 10. Δx = 7 − 1 = 6; Δy = 10 − 2 = 8 AB = √(6² + 8²) = 10 units

pyth-questions-014-answer.title: Subtract the negative coordinate carefully
pyth-questions-014-answer.alt: On a square coordinate grid, P is (−3, 1) and Q is (5, 7). Find PQ. 10 units: Δx = 5 − (−3) = 8 and Δy = 6; √(8² + 6²) = 10. Δx = 5 − (−3) = 8; Δy = 7 − 1 = 6 PQ = √(8² + 6²) = 10 units

pyth-questions-015-answer.title: “Rise” and “horizontal run” are the legs
pyth-questions-015-answer.alt: A straight ramp rises 0.9 m vertically over a horizontal run of 1.2 m. Find the ramp’s length. 1.5 m: the ramp is the hypotenuse, √(0.9² + 1.2²). L² = 0.9² + 1.2² = 2.25 L = 1.5 m

pyth-questions-016-answer.title: Ramp length is not horizontal run
pyth-questions-016-answer.alt: A straight ramp is 5 m long and rises 3 m vertically. Find its horizontal run. 4 m: run = √(5² − 3²). The 5 m ramp is the hypotenuse. run² = 5² − 3² = 16 run = 4 m

pyth-questions-016-question.title: Sketch the problem
pyth-questions-016-question.alt: A straight ramp is 5 m long and rises 3 m vertically. Find its horizontal run.

pyth-questions-017-answer.title: Translate the words before calculating
pyth-questions-017-answer.alt: A ramp rises 3 m over a horizontal run of 4 m. In “find the length of the ramp”, which triangle side is requested? The sloping hypotenuse, not the vertical rise or horizontal run. “Rise” is vertical; “run” is horizontal. “Ramp length” is the sloping hypotenuse.

pyth-questions-018-answer.title: Split the symmetric shape down the middle
pyth-questions-018-answer.alt: An isosceles tent cross-section has equal sloping sides 10 m and base 12 m. Find its perpendicular height. 8 m: the height halves the base to 6 m, so h = √(10² − 6²). Half the base: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m. h = √(10² − 6²) = 8 m

pyth-questions-019-answer.title: The altitude creates a right triangle
pyth-questions-019-answer.alt: Find the perpendicular height of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm, to one decimal place. 8.7 cm: half the base is 5 cm; h = √(10² − 5²) = √75 ≈ 8.6603. Half the base: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. h = √(10² − 5²) = √75 ≈ 8.7 cm

pyth-questions-020-answer.title: Use HALF of each diagonal
pyth-questions-020-answer.alt: A rhombus has diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm. They bisect each other at right angles. Find one side of the rhombus. 5 cm: use half-diagonals 3 cm and 4 cm as the legs; √(3² + 4²) = 5. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm; 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. side = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm

pyth-questions-021-answer.title: Find the perpendicular height first
pyth-questions-021-answer.alt: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 13 cm and base 10 cm. Find its area. 60 cm²: h = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm; area = ½ × 10 × 12. Half base = 5; h = √(13² − 5²) = 12. Area = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60 cm²

pyth-questions-022-answer.title: Use Pythagoras twice for a box
pyth-questions-022-answer.alt: Extension: a rectangular box measures 12 cm by 9 cm by 8 cm. Find the internal diagonal joining opposite corners through the box. 17 cm: base diagonal = 15 cm; space diagonal = √(15² + 8²) = 17. Base diagonal = √(12² + 9²) = 15 cm. Space diagonal = √(15² + 8²) = 17 cm.

pyth-questions-023-answer.title: “Shortest distance to a line” is perpendicular
pyth-questions-023-answer.alt: A tree is 10 m from a bench on a straight path. Its perpendicular foot on the path is 6 m from the bench. Find the shortest tree-to-path distance. 8 m: the shortest distance is perpendicular to the path, so √(10² − 6²) = 8. Tree-to-bench is the 10 m hypotenuse. Perpendicular distance = √(10² − 6²) = 8 m

pyth-questions-024-answer.title: “Around the boundary” means perimeter
steps: Follow all four sides, not a diagonal.
pyth-questions-024-answer.alt: A rectangular garden is 6 m by 8 m. How much fencing goes around its boundary? Decide whether Pythagoras is needed. 28 m: perimeter = 2(6 + 8). Pythagoras is unnecessary because no diagonal is requested. Follow all four sides, not a diagonal. Perimeter = 6 + 8 + 6 + 8 = 28 m

pyth-questions-025-answer.title: An angle is given—but it is not 90°
steps: 60° between the known sides does not qualify.
pyth-questions-025-answer.alt: Two sides of a triangle are 8 cm and 10 cm, with 60° between them. Why can’t you use 8² + 10² to find the third side’s square? The included angle is 60°, not 90°. Those sides are not perpendicular legs. Pythagoras needs a right triangle. 60° between the known sides does not qualify.

pyth-questions-026-answer.title: One side + an angle points to trigonometry
steps: Pythagoras alone needs another known side.
pyth-questions-026-answer.alt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 10 cm and an acute angle of 35°. Which method directly finds the opposite side, and why? Trigonometry: sine uses an angle and the hypotenuse. Pythagoras needs two known side lengths. sin 35° = opposite ÷ 10 Pythagoras alone needs another known side.

pyth-questions-027-answer.title: A parallelogram is not necessarily a rectangle
steps: The sides are not perpendicular here.
pyth-questions-027-answer.alt: A parallelogram has adjacent sides 6 cm and 8 cm and an included angle of 60°. Why can’t you assume its diagonal is 10 cm? A parallelogram need not have right angles. The 6–8–10 shortcut requires perpendicular 6 cm and 8 cm sides. The sides are not perpendicular here. “Diagonal” alone does not justify Pythagoras.

pyth-questions-028-answer.title: Equal sides do not guarantee a right angle
steps: You still need 90° BETWEEN those sides.
pyth-questions-028-answer.alt: An isosceles triangle has two 12 cm sides. What extra fact would justify using 12² + 12² to find its third side’s square? The angle between the two 12 cm sides must be 90°. Isosceles means two equal sides. You still need 90° BETWEEN those sides.

pyth-questions-029-answer.title: “Nearest tenth” means one decimal place
pyth-questions-029-answer.alt: A rectangular board is 5 cm by 7 cm. Find its diagonal to the nearest tenth of a centimetre. 8.6 cm: d = √74 ≈ 8.6023, rounded only at the end. d = √(5² + 7²) = √74 √74 ≈ 8.6023 → 8.6 cm

pyth-questions-030-answer.title: Mixed units: convert before squaring
pyth-questions-030-answer.alt: A 250 cm ladder leans against a vertical wall, with its foot 1.5 m away on level ground. Find its vertical reach in metres. 2 m: convert 250 cm to 2.5 m, then √(2.5² − 1.5²) = 2. 250 cm = 2.5 m; h² = 2.5² − 1.5². h = √4 = 2 m

pyth-questions-031-answer.title: “Corner-to-corner brace” means diagonal
pyth-questions-031-answer.alt: A rectangular gate is 2.4 m wide and 1.8 m high. Find the length of a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. 3 m: the brace is the diagonal; use 3–4–5 scaled by 0.6. (3, 4, 5) × 0.6 = (1.8, 2.4, 3) brace = √(1.8² + 2.4²) = 3 m

pyth-questions-032-answer.title: “Check it is square” can mean test 90°
steps: The 9 m and 12 m edges are perpendicular.
pyth-questions-032-answer.alt: A builder measures a triangular layout: 9 m, 12 m and 15 m. Explain how this checks whether the 9 m and 12 m edges meet at 90°. 9² + 12² = 15². The converse of Pythagoras confirms a right angle between the shorter edges. 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15² The 9 m and 12 m edges are perpendicular.
